note: Researched recommendations, written in the site's voice but by somebody who has not been. Opinionated on purpose — a list of facts is not a guide — but every card says plainly that it was researched rather than visited, and a handwritten note in notes.json overrules any of it. This file exists because nothing else can fill it: no open dataset in India describes everyday food, Wikidata holds two Delhi restaurants and no cafes, and the whole sourced tier here is monuments. See SOURCES.md.
rules: Every record needs a source and a lastVerified date. If it cannot be checked, it does not go in.
Say what to order and when to go. 'Lovely atmosphere' helps nobody.
No opening hours in prose. OpenStreetMap carries them, js/hours.js reads them, and a time written here is a time that rots.
quality and uniqueness cap at 4 here. 5 is reserved for somewhere one of you actually loved.
Where a claim is disputed, say it is disputed. Delhi has more than one restaurant claiming to have invented the same dish and at least one of those arguments is in court.

Always pin `match` with a zone. Matching on name alone resolved 'Bukhara' to a restaurant in Noida rather than the one in Chanakyapuri — and the famous one is not in OpenStreetMap at all, so the record was dropped. That is the index doing its job: it is what stops a writer inventing a place.

items.title: Karim's
items.why: Founded in 1913 near the Jama Masjid by Haji Karimuddin, whose family had cooked for the Mughal court, and often called Old Delhi's most famous place to eat. The menu is Mughlai: nihari, kebabs, korma, biryani.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Moti Mahal
items.why: The Daryaganj restaurant Kundan Lal Gujral opened after Partition, one of the first to bring Punjabi food like tandoori chicken, dal makhani and butter chicken to a wide audience. Order the tandoori chicken.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Indian Accent
items.why: Rohit Khattar's modern Indian restaurant, opened in 2009 at The Manor and at The Lodhi hotel since 2017, with sister restaurants in New York and Mumbai. Book well ahead for the tasting menu.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Saravana Bhavan
items.why: The Connaught Place branch of the Chennai-based South Indian vegetarian chain, which has grown to dozens of outlets in India and abroad. Come for a dosa and filter coffee.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lodhi Gardens
items.why: Ninety acres with eleven monuments standing in it — the tombs of Muhammad Shah Sayyid (1444) and Sikandar Lodi, the Bada Gumbad, the Shish Gumbad — laid out as a garden around them in 1936. Delhi walks here in the morning. The octagonal Sayyid tomb is the one to look at properly: Hindu features built into an Indo-Islamic building.
items.source: Wikipedia; Incredible India; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sunder Nursery
items.why: Ninety acres next to Humayun's Tomb, derelict for decades and reopened in 2018 after a ten-year restoration by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture — the charbagh canals rebuilt, the axis to the tomb restored, hundreds of native species planted as Delhi's first arboretum. Six World Heritage monuments stand inside it. Time put it on its list of the world's hundred greatest places that year.
items.source: Wikipedia; Aga Khan Development Network; Delhi Tourism; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Agrasen ki Baoli
items.why: A historical stepwell, 60 metres long and 15 wide, set among the office blocks off Hailey Road near Connaught Place. Go on a quiet weekday morning.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Bahrisons Booksellers
items.why: The Khan Market bookshop Balraj Bahri Malhotra opened in 1953 after Partition, raising the money by selling one of his mother's gold bangles. Still run by the family.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A Khan Market café of the Gurugram-based roaster, which buys from more than eighty Indian coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Bengali Sweet House
items.why: A sweet shop in Bengali Market, one of New Delhi's oldest markets, built in 1930 by Bengali Mal Lohia — the name has nothing to do with Bengal. Buy a box of sweets to take away.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Khari Baoli Spice Market
items.why: Asia's largest wholesale spice market, trading since the seventeenth century by the Fatehpuri Masjid at the western end of Chandni Chowk, selling spices, nuts, herbs, rice and tea. Go early.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lajpat Nagar Central Market
items.why: The central market of Lajpat Nagar, the South Delhi neighbourhood named after Lala Lajpat Rai. Clothes, fabric, shoes and household goods; evenings are busiest.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); Delhi Tourism; position from OpenStreetMap
items.imageCredit: Ville Miettinen from Helsinki, Finland · CC BY 2.0

items.title: Nai Sarak Bookshop Area
items.why: Nai Sarak, the 'new street' between Chandni Chowk and Chawri Bazaar, is a wholesale and retail market for school and college textbooks. Walk it after a paratha in the lane next door.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Wenger's
items.why: One of the first shops in Connaught Place. It began in 1926 at Kashmere Gate, run by a Swiss couple who introduced Delhi to pastries and Swiss chocolates, and still bakes its own breads and cakes.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: L'Opera
items.why: A French bakery near Khan Market that makes its own viennoiserie, macarons, pastries and breads. Stop for a croissant or a box of macarons.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Cafe Lota
items.why: The café inside the National Crafts Museum, opposite Purana Qila, cooking regional Indian food. See the museum first, then have lunch.
items.source: Our own visit; national Crafts Museum; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kunzum Travel Cafe
items.why: A Hauz Khas Village café built around books and travel, with its own book club and reading events. Come to read over a coffee.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Subko Cafe
items.why: The Lodhi Colony café of Subko, a specialty coffee roaster that also makes fine cacao and runs a craft bakehouse. Order a coffee and something from the bakery counter.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A Chittaranjan Park café of the Gurugram-based roaster, which buys from more than eighty Indian coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Indian Coffee House
items.why: A branch of the Indian Coffee House, the chain run by worker co-operatives since the first outlet opened in Bombay in 1936. Cheap coffee and snacks in a room with history.
items.source: Our own visit; wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Bahrisons Booksellers
items.why: The Khan Market bookshop Balraj Bahri Malhotra opened in 1953, a refugee from Partition who sold a gold bangle for the capital. Still run by the family.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Another Fine Day

match.name: Another Fine Day Cafe and Reading Room

items.why: A café tucked into Gurugram's corporate blocks, with an all-day breakfast menu, mezze, grills, sandwiches and wraps. Good alone with a book or with company.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A Malviya Nagar café of the Gurugram-based roaster, which buys from more than eighty Indian coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Moti Mahal Delux
items.why: A branch of the chain descended from Kundan Lal Gujral's Moti Mahal in Daryaganj, the restaurant credited with popularising tandoori chicken, butter chicken and dal makhani. Order those.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: United Coffee House
items.why: One of Connaught Place's early restaurants, where Jawaharlal Nehru came to hear the poet Josh Malihabadi at its mushairas. Continental and Mughlai food in an old-fashioned room.
items.source: Our own visit; wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Khan Market home of Delhi's Big Chill café chain, which now runs three places in the market including its own cakery. Italian food, long dessert list.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Guppy
items.why: AD Singh's Japanese-themed restaurant in Lodhi Colony, from the restaurateur behind Olive. Book for dinner.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Colocal
items.why: A chocolate maker selling bars made from Indian-origin cacao, like its 55 per cent single-origin dark, plus cookies and coffee. Buy a bar to take home.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: One8 commune
items.why: Virat Kohli's restaurant and bar in Worldmark 2: Asian, Italian and North Indian on one menu, an outdoor lounge, and cocktails until late. Order the signature black chicken.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Chache di Hatti
items.why: The Kamla Nagar chole bhature shop that draws very long queues during its short opening hours. Get there early.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kallu Nihari
items.why: A shop in Old Delhi that has served nothing but nihari, a slow-cooked meat stew, since Mohammed Rafiquddin — Kallu Mian — opened it in 1990. Go early; it sells out.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Arsalan Restaurant & Caterer
items.why: The Delhi branch of Arsalan, the Kolkata restaurant known for its Kolkata-style biryani. Order the biryani.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Farzi Cafe
items.why: A Cyber Hub branch of Farzi Café, one of Zorawar Kalra's modern Indian restaurant brands. Good for a group dinner.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Ladurée
items.why: The Khan Market shop and tearoom of Ladurée, the Paris pastry house founded in 1862 on the rue Royale and best known for macarons. Buy a box to take away.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Game On Board
items.why: Delhi's first board-game café, with a library of more than 500 games and game masters to teach them, plus food and drink. Bring friends and stay a few hours.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Piano Man New Delhi
items.why: The Eldeco Centre stage of The Piano Man, Delhi's best-known jazz club, with live music most nights. Book tickets for the show you want.
items.source: Our own visit; the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Kailash Colony café of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Saket branch of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: L'Opera
items.why: A Vasant Vihar shop of L'Opéra, the French bakery making its own viennoiserie, macarons, pastries and breads. Stop for a croissant.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Call Me Ten
items.why: A Japanese restaurant in Basant Lok, opened in 2024 by a group of founders including actor Neha Sharma. Good for sushi and small plates at dinner.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Vasant Kunj branch of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kwality
items.why: One of the early Connaught Place restaurants, which brought Continental and Mughlai cooking to the plaza. An old-fashioned room for lunch.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Big Chill
items.why: The Connaught Place branch of the Big Chill, Delhi's own café chain. Italian food and a long dessert list.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Devan's at Lodhi
items.why: A Lodhi Colony shop of Devan's, the coffee and tea merchant selling single-origin coffees, blends and teas from Darjeeling, Assam and the Nilgiris. Buy freshly ground coffee.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Jalebi Wala
items.why: The Old Famous Jalebi Wala at the Dariba Kalan corner of Chandni Chowk, frying crisp jalebis. Buy them hot, by weight.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Dhaba
items.why: Dhaba by Claridges, a restaurant themed on a Punjabi highway dhaba, cooking rustic North Indian food. Order dal and something from the tandoor.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Another Fine Day
items.why: A café in Gurugram's corporate blocks with an all-day breakfast menu, mezze, grills, sandwiches and wraps. Good alone with a book or with company.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: INJA
items.why: Indian cooking through a Japanese lens, in the house at The Manor where Indian Accent began. The tasting menu is dinner only and the reason to come, so book weeks ahead for a weekend. It's closed on Tuesdays.
items.source: The Manor's own dining page

items.title: Megu
items.why: The Leela's Japanese room, grilling over binchō-tan charcoal with produce flown in from Tokyo's markets. Order from the grill, or book the small omakase counter for a special night. It's a hotel dining room at hotel prices, at its best for a long dinner.
items.source: The Leela's own press releases

items.title: Perch
items.why: A narrow first-floor room in Khan Market that does serious coffee by day and wine by the glass after dark. Come mid-afternoon for a pour-over and the window seats over the market lane.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: AMA Cafe
items.area: Majnu ka Tilla, New Aruna Nagar
items.why: The best-known café in Majnu ka Tilla, the Tibetan colony on the Yamuna: several floors of students and monks over coffee, cheesecake and Tibetan bread. Pair it with laphing from the lane stalls outside.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Diggin
items.why: A garden café in Chanakyapuri, all fairy lights and outdoor tables, serving pasta, pizza and cold coffee to students and families. Best on a winter afternoon.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Carnatic Café
items.why: Karnataka breakfast done properly: thin, crisp, ghee-roasted dosas with podi and filter coffee in a steel tumbler. Order the benne masala dosa and a kesari bath.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mum Café and Bakery
items.why: A small neighbourhood café and bakery in Moti Bagh, good for a slow breakfast with something just out of the oven.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Tibetan Food Stop
items.why: A cheap Tibetan counter in Vasant Vihar: steamed momos, thukpa and thenthuk, for less than a coffee costs a few doors down.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Andhra Bhawan Canteen
items.why: The state guesthouse canteen on Ashoka Road, where civil servants and students queue for the unlimited Andhra thali on steel plates: rice, sambar, rasam, pickles and gunpowder ghee, refilled until you stop them. Sunday's chicken and mutton fry draws the biggest line.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Himachal Bhawan Dining Hall
items.why: Another state-bhawan canteen, this one serving Himachali home food — madra, siddu, and the Sunday dham — for very little. Go at lunchtime.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Gulati
items.why: The longest-running of the Pandara Road restaurants, a short row near India Gate famous for Punjabi food served late into the night. Order the butter chicken and dal makhani with garlic naan, and share.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Paranthe Wala, Paranthe Wali Gali

match.name: Pandit Kanhaiya Lal Durga Prashad Dixit Paranthe Wala

items.why: One of the last of the family shops that named Paranthe Wali Gali, open since 1875 according to the sign. Parathas here are deep-fried in ghee, not griddled, and stuffed with anything from rabri to bitter gourd; they come with pumpkin sabzi, banana-tamarind chutney and pickle.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Natraj Dahi Bhalle Wala
items.why: A hatch on the corner of Chandni Chowk selling two things: dahi bhalla, soft lentil dumplings in cold sweet curd and tamarind, and aloo tikki. Eat standing on the step.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Jung Bahadur Kachori Wala
items.why: Since 1961 near Paranthe Wali Gali: urad-dal kachori, crisp and hollow, with a tangy aloo sabzi. A good first stop before the bigger plates.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Burma Burma
items.why: Vegetarian Burmese at Select Citywalk: khow suey with all its crunchy toppings, tea-leaf salad and bubble tea. The best case in south Delhi for a meatless dinner nobody complains about.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nagaland's Kitchen
items.why: Naga food in Green Park: smoked pork with bamboo shoot, axone and raja mirchi chutney. Fiery and fermented; order rice and go easy at first.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Yeti
items.why: Himalayan food — Nepali, Tibetan and Bhutanese — upstairs in Connaught Place. Go for the thakali thali, jhol momos and ema datshi.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Jamun
items.why: Regional Indian cooking in a bungalow off Lodhi Road, with dishes taken from home kitchens across the country rather than the usual restaurant canon. Ask what is new on the seasonal menu.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Khan Chacha
items.why: The roll counter in Khan Market that started as a kebab stall: a chicken or paneer tikka roll in rumali roti, eaten standing up in the lane.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Annapurna Bhojnalai
items.why: A cheap vegetarian dining room by North Campus where students eat thalis between classes.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Giani's di Hatti
items.why: The original Giani's, in Fatehpuri at the west end of Chandni Chowk, where the Delhi chain began. The order is rabri-falooda: cold vermicelli, thick reduced milk and kulfi in one glass.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kuremal Mohanlal Kulfiwale
items.why: A kulfi shop in the lanes of Chawri Bazar, famous for kulfis frozen inside the hollowed-out fruit — mango, orange, pomegranate — and sliced to order. Several branches of the family use the Kuremal name; this is the one in the old lanes.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Roshan Di Kulfi
items.why: A Karol Bagh institution on Ajmal Khan Road, known for kesar-pista kulfi and, in winter, gajar ka halwa. Pair it with the chole bhature they also serve.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nathu's Sweets
items.why: The Bengali Market sweet shop, around since the 1930s: barfi, besan laddoo and, in winter, moong dal halwa. Busy with box orders before every festival.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lokenath Sweets
items.why: A CR Park sweet shop for Bengali mishti: rosogolla, sandesh and mishti doi in clay pots. Best in the evening, after the fish market.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Annapurna Sweets
items.why: A Bengali sweet shop in Green Park: notun gurer sandesh in winter, and rosogolla all year.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Oberoi Patisserie
items.area: The Oberoi, Dr Zakir Hussain Marg
items.why: The pastry shop at The Oberoi on Dr Zakir Hussain Marg: laminated pastries, macarons and celebration cakes at hotel prices. The place to buy a cake that has to impress.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Chocolateria San Churro
items.why: Churros with thick Spanish hot chocolate for dipping, in CR Park. A good stop on a winter evening.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Si, Si! Gelato
items.why: A small gelateria in Vasant Kunj for Italian-style gelato in rotating flavours.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Bahrisons at Galleria
items.why: Bahrisons, the Khan Market booksellers, opened this Gurugram branch in Galleria Market with a café inside, so you can read before you buy.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sibang Bakery
items.why: A Korean bakery in the Sector 53 market, where Gurugram's Korean community shops: soft milk bread, red-bean buns, castella and iced Americanos.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Bibimbab
items.why: One of the small Korean restaurants in the Sector 53 market: dolsot bibimbap in a sizzling stone bowl, kimchi jjigae and banchan that keeps coming.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Midam
items.why: Korean home cooking next door to The Bibimbab: tteokbokki, japchae and a seafood pancake to share.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kashgar
items.why: Inside Lotus Villas in DLF Phase IV: a slow-cooked Mughlai menu of kebabs, nihari and biryani, for when you can't face the drive to Old Delhi.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Le Truffle
items.why: A small patisserie in DLF Phase IV for tarts, entremets and cakes to order.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Smoor
items.why: A Bengaluru chocolatier's Gurugram branch: plated desserts, hot chocolate and boxed chocolates to take away.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Cafe Turtle
items.why: Upstairs from the Full Circle bookshop in Khan Market: a quiet café for coffee, cake and the paperback you just bought. Ask for a table by the window.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lavonne Cafe
items.why: The café of a Bengaluru baking academy, in Defence Colony market: laminated pastries, tarts and a proper brunch.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Madras Coffee House
items.why: An old-fashioned South Indian coffee room in Connaught Place's Inner Circle: filter coffee, idli-vada and dosa at prices from another decade.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Dada & Bodi Tandoori Tea Stall
items.why: A CR Park stall for tandoori chai: tea poured into a clay kulhad still hot from the tandoor, so it boils up and turns smoky. Ten minutes and a few rupees.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: JugMug Thela
items.why: A roadside stall in Saidulajab with a far longer tea and coffee list than its size suggests, from masala chai to cold brews. Stand at the counter and ask what's new.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Ssongchee
items.why: A Korean dessert café near Saket for bingsu: a bowl of feather-light shaved milk ice heaped with mango, injeolmi or red bean. Share one between two.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Altogether Experimental
items.why: A café that doubles as an art and workshop space in Lado Sarai's gallery lanes. Check what is on the walls before you order.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kenangan Coffee
items.why: The Indonesian chain's Delhi café: try the es kopi susu, iced coffee sweetened with palm sugar.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Madison and Pike
items.why: A New York-style all-day café in Nirvana Courtyard, Sector 50: big brunches, good coffee and a covered terrace.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: BBR Coffee

match.name: BBR Coffee by Before British Raj

items.why: A café from Before British Raj, an Indian estate-coffee brand: single-estate pour-overs and bags of beans to take home.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Dark Brown, World Street
items.why: A café on World Street for coffee, shakes and something chocolatey between laps of the themed streets.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: World Street, Faridabad
items.why: An open-air high street built as a world tour, with themed streets lined with London-, Paris- and other city-style façades and cafés and restaurants below. It is liveliest in the evening, when the lights come on. Coffee at Blue Tokai, then dinner on London Street.
items.source: Omaxe; trade press

items.title: Blue Tokai, World Street
items.why: Faridabad's branch of the Gurugram-based specialty roaster, open since December 2024: Indian single-estate coffee and the best espresso on World Street.
items.source: Trade press (India Retailing, Dec 2024)

items.title: Kiran Nadar Museum of Art
items.why: India's first private museum of modern and contemporary art, in a mall basement in Saket of all places: Husain, Souza, Gaitonde and Amrita Sher-Gil, with rotating contemporary shows. Entry is free; go on a weekday afternoon.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Khirki Masjid
items.why: A fourteenth-century Tughlaq mosque, unusually roofed over, its name from the latticed khirkis (windows) in its walls. It stands in Khirki village, opposite the Saket malls, and you will often have it to yourself.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mahabelly
items.why: Kerala food in Saket: appam with stew, Malabar parotta with beef or chicken fry, and fish curry with red rice. A good lunch after KNMA.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: CoCo Ichibanya
items.why: The Japanese curry-rice chain at Select Citywalk: pick a base, a topping and a spice level from one to ten, and start lower than you think.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Garden of Five Senses
items.why: Twenty acres of rock garden, water features, bamboo and flower beds on the ridge at Saidulajab, laid out by the Delhi tourism corporation for the senses rather than the eye alone. Best in February, for the flower show, or on a winter afternoon.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mahabelly Canteen
items.why: The quicker, cheaper sibling of Mahabelly in Saidulajab's lanes: Kerala meals, parotta and beef fry, and filter coffee.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Ganga Dhaba
items.why: JNU's best-known dhaba, open late: chai, parathas and Maggi on stone seats under the trees, with half the campus's arguments going on around you. It is inside the university, so go with somebody from JNU or check entry rules at the gate.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sabarmati Dhaba
items.why: The hostel dhaba by Sabarmati in JNU, for late tea and cheap thalis between Ganga Dhaba and the hostel lawns.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: PVR Priya
items.why: The Basant Lok single-screen cinema that gave PVR its name: Priya Village Roadshow began here. Now a modern screen, but still the anchor of the market.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Manam Chocolate
items.why: The Hyderabad bean-to-bar chocolate maker's first café outside Hyderabad: hot chocolates, shakes and plated desserts made from Indian cacao, and bars to take home.
items.source: Researched; venue's own pages

items.title: 6 Ballygunge Place
items.why: A Delhi branch of the Kolkata restaurant known for Bengali home cooking: shukto, kosha mangsho, bhetki paturi steamed in banana leaf, and mishti doi to finish.
items.source: Researched; venue's own pages

items.title: Hikki
items.why: Japanese at Eldeco Centre: sushi, robata and small plates for a slower dinner before a drink next door.
items.source: Researched; venue's own pages

items.title: The Mission Bay
items.why: Mexican food by way of San Francisco, with a bar: burritos, tacos and margaritas, the loudest room in the building.
items.source: Researched; venue's own pages

items.title: Sukiya
items.why: The Japanese gyudon chain's Nehru Place branch: a bowl of thin-sliced beef, or chicken, simmered with onion over rice, with miso soup and a raw or soft egg on the side. Quick, cheap and better than the food court.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Juggernaut
items.why: Andhra and South Indian thalis in Kailash Colony market: rice with podi and ghee, pappu, gongura and a fiery chicken fry. Come hungry for the lunch thali.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nimtho
items.why: Sikkimese and Himalayan cooking near GK I: momos, thukpa, gundruk soup and a Sikkimese thali. One of the few places in the city for food from Sikkim.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: 34, Chowringhee Lane
items.why: Kolkata-style kathi rolls in CR Park, named after the Calcutta street: an egg-chicken roll with onion and green chilli is the order.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Gopal's Chop and Cutlet
items.why: A CR Park snack counter for Bengali telebhaja: fish fry, chicken cutlet, vegetable chop and mochar chop, fried to order with kasundi on the side.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Epicuria, Nehru Place
items.why: A food-and-drink mall built over Nehru Place metro: Delhi favourites like Karim's and Khan Chacha in one building, bars including The Irish House and Social, and an INOX Insignia cinema upstairs. Easiest after work, straight off the Violet Line. For a sit-down dinner, Fio Cookhouse is the pick; for something quick, walk to Sukiya.
items.source: OpenStreetMap (venues in the building)

items.title: Fio Cookhouse & Bar
items.why: The city sibling of Fio at the Garden of Five Senses, opened in Epicuria in 2013: a European-leaning menu and a proper bar, and the most grown-up dinner in the building. Book for a table after work, straight off the Violet Line.
items.source: Delhi Tourism listing; restaurant press

items.title: Fio Country Kitchen & Bar
items.area: Gate 1, Garden of Five Senses, Saidulajab
items.why: The original Fio, inside the Garden of Five Senses: tables out among the trees and lanterns, a European menu and a bar. Best on a winter evening, after a walk round the garden.
items.source: Restaurant press; listings for address only

items.title: Dolma Aunty Momos
items.why: A momo counter in Lajpat Nagar Central Market, one of the stalls that made momos a Delhi street food in the 1990s. Steamed pork or chicken, with the fiery red chutney; eat them standing between the shopping bags.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nagpal Chole Bhature
items.why: A Lajpat Nagar IV shop that does chole bhature and little else: a puffed bhatura, dark, tangy chole and pickled onions. Mornings are best, before the weekend queue builds.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Hunger Strike
items.why: The Amar Colony market counter for pav bhaji, chole kulche and cheese-loaded sandwiches. Messy, buttery and cheap; good after shopping.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sanjay Chur Chur Naan
items.why: Amritsari-style chur chur naan: a crisp, flaky stuffed naan crushed by hand and doused in butter, served with chole and chutney.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Japan Foundation, New Delhi
items.why: Japan's cultural centre in Delhi: a library of Japanese books and films, language courses, and free film screenings and talks. Check the events page before you go.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sagar Ratna, Defence Colony
items.why: The first Sagar Ratna, opened here in 1986 before it became a chain across north India. Order the Mysore masala dosa, a rava idli and filter coffee.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Defence Bakery
items.why: The old bakery in Defence Colony market, a neighbourhood fixture for decades: chicken patties, cream rolls and a birthday cake to order. Get the patties warm.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Moets
items.why: A long-running, family-run restaurant complex in the market, with several kitchens under one name. Go for the North Indian: kebabs, butter chicken and naan, with a big group.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Angels in My Kitchen
items.why: A small bakery-café in the market for cakes, cupcakes and cookies, and a cake to order for someone else.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Amici
items.why: Thin-crust pizzas and simple pasta in the market: a dependable Italian dinner with no fuss.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Aka Gaka
items.why: A small Japanese place in the market for ramen, donburi and sushi rolls.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mubarak Shah Sayyid's Tomb
items.why: The octagonal tomb of the second Sayyid sultan, built in 1434, now surrounded by the lanes of Kotla Mubarakpur village. With two Lodi-era gumbads nearby, it's a ten-minute walk from Defence Colony market into fifteenth-century Delhi.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Anna Maya
items.why: The all-day food hall at the Andaz: a bakery counter, a pantry of Indian produce and a menu built around regional, seasonal ingredients. The best breakfast in Aerocity if you have a flight to wait for.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Dhaba Estd 1986
items.why: A Punjabi highway dhaba recreated in Worldmark, with truck art on the walls and butter chicken, dal and tandoori on the menu. A loud, easy dinner for a group.
items.source: Researched; position and hours from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Worldmark, Aerocity
items.area: Aerocity, by the Airport Express metro
items.why: The block of glass towers between Aerocity's hotels that has become a dining district: dozens of restaurants, bars and cafés on open walkways, busy with office crowds after work and travellers killing time before a flight. Easiest by Airport Express metro.
items.source: OpenStreetMap; researched

items.title: Dragonfly Experience
items.why: Pan-Asian and modern Indian, biryani included, in a dim room themed on dragonflies, with a long cocktail list and a soundtrack that builds as the night goes on. Good for a long dinner that turns into drinks.
items.source: Your notes; researched, not visited

items.title: Monsoon
items.why: Contemporary Indian built on home-style regional cooking: a Kerala mappas prawn curry, mutton gujiya, and a blue-tea mojito. Slower and quieter than the bars around it.
items.source: Your notes; researched, not visited

items.title: Kuuraku Ramen
items.why: Proper miso and shoyu ramen with gyoza, in the lower-ground food court. Quick and cheap if you don't want fine dining before a flight.
items.source: Your notes; researched, not visited

items.title: Blue Tokai, GMR Square
items.why: The specialty roaster's Aerocity café, open early and late, so it works between flights: a vanilla-bean iced latte and sourdough toast.
items.source: Your notes; researched, not visited

items.title: Chai Garam
items.why: Masala chai made by hand, lassi and wraps in the Worldmark 1 food court: the cheap, quick stop between flights.
items.source: Your notes; researched, not visited
